parameters.description: Label-only entry context recorded on every hypothesis for one identical workflow; it never changes gate precedence, evidence states, ranking, or outputs.
parameters.name: entry-mode

analysis.purpose: Validate one rare-disease case bundle and rank its established disease-gene hypotheses by explicit evidence state.
workflow: Validate the case bundle fail-closed: check required files, parse the phenopacket, enforce controlled vocabularies, case_id agreement, and transcript presence on consequence-bearing rows, and reject with a named field before writing any output.
Resolve every cited evidence identifier against the manifest, separating resolved supporting/contradicting evidence from absent or unresolvable identifiers.

Evaluate each disease-gene hypothesis through the deterministic gate cascade (hard-stop abstentions, then contradictions, then missing-evidence blockers, else concordant), counting independent evidence lines with correlated predictors collapsed by predictor group.
Rank hypotheses by evidence state then independent evidence support, compute source-version provenance, and compute the optional reanalysis diff against a supplied prior dossier.
Write the ranked hypotheses table, the evidence dossier, the reanalysis diff, and the per-hypothesis evidence-completeness figure.

caveats.text: Inputs describe an ESTABLISHED disease-gene relationship with pre-annotated nuclear germline SNVs/indels; the skill never establishes a novel gene-disease association from a single case or publication.
Research decision support only: it emits evidence states, contradictions, missing-evidence codes, and abstentions, never a diagnosis, a diagnostic probability, or an ACMG/AMP classification.
Variant classes beyond snv/indel, and any hypothesis whose cited evidence cannot be resolved, are abstained rather than forced through SNV/indel logic.

A concordant evidence state is not a clinical result. Canonical runtime checks establish artifact integrity and accounting; report interpretation, citation compliance and visual quality require external inspection and acceptance.

description: Use to prioritize established rare-disease disease-gene hypotheses for one case by running a deterministic, fail-closed evidence-gating cascade that assigns each hypothesis an explicit evidence state with contradictions, missing-evidence codes, abstentions, provenance, and an optional reanalysis diff.

guidance.use_when: you need the exact gate precedence, evidence-state definitions, and reason-code vocabulary behind each ranked hypothesis
before preparing report facts, citations, the infographic, or any PDF narrative; its exact bibliography and research-only rules are mandatory
migrating an existing invocation or interpreting which checks the canonical runner owns

reject_if: A required file is missing or unreadable, the phenopacket is malformed, its metaData.phenopacketSchemaVersion is missing/empty/not schema major version 2, or its subject id is unresolved.
A candidates.tsv row uses an out-of-vocabulary value, disagrees with the phenopacket case_id, or omits a transcript_id on a consequence-bearing row.
The evidence manifest has a row with an empty evidence_id or a duplicate evidence_id.
A supplied prior evidence dossier does not match this case by schema or case_id.
requirements: Provide phenopacket.json using GA4GH Phenopacket schema major version 2, whose top-level id is the case identifier and whose subject has a resolvable id.
Provide candidates.tsv with the full controlled-vocabulary column set, one row per allele, every row's case_id equal to the phenopacket id, and a transcript_id on every consequence-bearing row.
Provide evidence_manifest.tsv that declares every cited evidence_id exactly once (no duplicate rows) with its source_type, version_or_date, and verification_status.
Assert an absent phenotype only with excluded:true; a term that is simply not listed is unknown, never absent.
input.summary: One case-bundle directory: a GA4GH Phenopacket (phenopacket.json), a candidate disease-gene hypotheses table (candidates.tsv), and an evidence manifest (evidence_manifest.tsv); with optional family.tsv, phenotype-state-companion.json, and a prior evidence dossier for reanalysis.

objective: Assign every candidate disease-gene hypothesis a transparent, reproducible evidence state (concordant, incomplete, conflicting, or abstained) with explicit reason codes, ranking, and provenance, so a human expert can decide where to focus follow-up -- without emitting a diagnosis, a diagnostic probability, or a formal variant classification.

sources.name: Supplied case evidence
sources.use: Offline declarative evidence and source-version provenance; verification_status is supplied evidence metadata, not proof of a new external verification.

sources.name: Pinned standards and methodology bibliography
sources.use: Required numbered report citations; no network retrieval, substitutions or added sources.

starting_prompt: Prioritize the established disease-gene hypotheses for this rare-disease case and explain each evidence state?
